# Giorgi Suramlishvili

Personal project site of Giorgi Suramlishvili, a sixth-form (A-Level) student in Bristol, UK. He designs and builds his own devices: hardware, firmware, 3D-printed enclosures, PCBs and the app that controls them.

- Site: https://giorgi.uk/
- Email: suramgiorgi10@gmail.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/giors1000
- Based in: Bristol, UK (born in Tbilisi, Georgia). Speaks English and Georgian.
- Tools: Fusion 360, KiCad, C++ on ESP32 (ESP32-C6, ESP32-S3), Python, MATLAB, 3D printing, MQTT, Firebase, Web Bluetooth.
- A-Levels: Maths, Further Maths, Physics, Computer Science.
- Last updated: October 2026.

## Projects

### 1. Smart light switch (2022 to 2023, finished after three versions)
https://giorgi.uk/projects/light-switch.html
A box that sits over a normal UK wall switch and presses it with an SG90 servo, so the mains wiring is never touched. ESP32-C6, LD2410C 24 GHz mmWave radar for presence (it notices people sitting still), two TTP223 touch pads, an SSD1306 OLED, five modes (Auto, Manual, Alarm, Bedtime, Locked), local sleep-habit scoring using a circular mean of bedtimes, MQTT, Bluetooth setup and recovery, Alexa and Google Home through SinricPro, OpenWeatherMap, dual-slot settings storage, safe mode and update rollback. Started when he was 13.

### 2. Blinds controller (2025, version 1)
https://giorgi.uk/projects/blinds-control.html
A stepper motor that pulls the bead chain of an existing roller blind. ESP32-C6, TMC2209 driver (StealthChop2, 20 kHz timer interrupt for steps), custom KiCad PCB, 3D-printed case, one TTP223 touch pad with a gesture state machine, five on-device automations (morning wake-up, close at sunset, night lock, close when the room is empty using the light switch's occupancy over MQTT, heat protection).

### 3. Zaylo Remote (2025 to 2026)
https://giorgi.uk/projects/zaylo-remote.html
An installable web app (PWA) that controls the light switch and blinds. Live device state over MQTT WebSockets, Firebase sign-in and shared homes with invites, a Web Bluetooth setup and rescue flow for devices that lose Wi-Fi, a diagnostics screen, and a demo mode with simulated devices that runs on the page.

### 4. Atlas, a self-balancing desk robot (2025 to 2026, built and balancing; documentation in progress)
https://giorgi.uk/projects/self-balancing-robot.html
His A-Level Computer Science project. A two-wheeled robot on an ESP32-S3 that balances using an LQR (linear quadratic regulator) controller. It started as a PID design; it now uses LQR, with the robot modelled in state-space form from Newton's laws, Q and R chosen with Bryson's rule, and the gain vector K solved in MATLAB. Parts: MPU-6500 IMU, JGA25-370 geared motors with encoders, DRV8833 motor driver, VL53L0X distance sensor, TCRT5000 edge sensor, GC9A01 round display, MAX98357A amplifier. The balance loop runs as its own FreeRTOS task. It is also a revision timer: the round screen counts down study sessions while it balances. He is now writing up the documentation.

### 5. Controlling an inverted pendulum (2026, paper)
https://giorgi.uk/projects/inverted-pendulum.html
A 16-page paper covering PID control (including integral windup, clamping and noise), then a derivation of LQR for a two-wheeled robot: the state vector, deriving the A and B matrices with the small-angle approximation, eigenvalues and stability, full-state feedback u = -Kx, controllability, why pole placement falls short, the cost function with Q and R, and the continuous algebraic Riccati equation. The worked example gives K = [-1.0, -2.0, 24.6, 3.07] with closed-loop eigenvalues -13.63, -6.07 and -0.84 +/- 0.50i.

Work experience week covering engineering, project management, advanced manufacturing and aviation safety. Visited the CTF where composite fan blades for UltraFan are made, attended a seminar on aviation safety investigations, worked in a team of five on a pitch for making STEM accessible to more people, presented to Rolls-Royce engineers, and finished at Aerospace Bristol (piston engines through to the Olympus 593 and an Adour Mk102).
